body:
Texas Pacific Group (TPG), a global private equity fund (PEF) manager acquiring Lotte Rental, the No. 1 rental car company in Korea, has entered the home stretch to switch to acquisition financing with borrowings. The plan is to complete the acquisition entirely with equity and then pursue acquisition financing, and it is expected to move to secure additional equity.

According to the investment banking (IB) industry on the 30th, TPG recently met with major domestic financial institutions, including commercial banks, and began talks to raise acquisition financing for Lotte Rental. The structure calls for the special-purpose company (SPC) established for the Lotte Rental acquisition to take on the borrowing, and Woori Bank is seen as the leading candidate to serve as the sole arranger.

In Aug., TPG signed a stock purchase agreement (SPA) to buy 61.18% equity in Lotte Rental held by Hotel Lotte and Busan Lotte Hotel for about 1.3 trillion won. Through SPC Lexicon Korea Holdco, it will acquire only existing shares without issuing new shares, and it also announced a plan to fund the acquisition price entirely with equity.

The transaction closing is expected as early as next month. This is because, based on the SPA signing date, the Korea Fair Trade Commission approved TPG's acquisition of Lotte Rental shares in early this month, about 13 business days later, leaving only follow-up procedures such as the shareholders' meeting. Lotte Rental is expected to hold an extraordinary shareholders' meeting on the 27th of next month.

Analysts say TPG is accelerating the shift in its acquisition funding structure. TPG's push for an all-equity acquisition is known as a strategic choice to respond to the Lotte Group's desire for swift cash procurement from the sale of Lotte Rental. With the SPA signed, the all-equity card has done its job.

In fact, the Lotte Group pursued the sale of Lotte Rental as a way to improve the group's financial soundness. In particular, as of the end of June, Hotel Lotte's consolidated borrowings and bonds exceeded 7 trillion won. The Lotte Group highly valued that TPG could pay the acquisition price within the year without separate financing.

Although the size of the borrowing and the timing of the drawdown have not yet been decided, TPG is expected to use the borrowed funds to secure additional equity. It is said to be reviewing a plan to immediately pursue a tender offer for Lotte Rental. The SPC would use the borrowed funds it raised as tender offer funds instead of returning them to the fund.

Expanding equity is cited as a way to overcome the limitations of a 61.18% equity structure secured through existing shares. Lotte Rental is listed on the main board, and the remaining roughly 39% belongs to minority shareholders. For the SPC to pay interest on its borrowing, it has no choice but to rely on Lotte Rental dividends, and dividends are paid to minority shareholders in proportion to their equity stakes.

An IB industry source said, "TPG is pursuing a so-called 'post-LBO (leveraged buyout)' strategy, securing deal certainty with its own capital first and restoring leverage afterward," and added, "TPG is expected to increase equity through a subsequent tender offer, then proceed with a voluntary delisting to reduce dividend leakage."
